scenes.title: Secrets & Config Management
scenes.narration: Secrets management stores sensitive values like database passwords and API keys securely, so they never end up hardcoded in your code or config files.

scenes.title: Why Not Hardcode Secrets
bullets: Secrets in code end up in version control history forever, even after you delete them.
A dedicated secrets store encrypts values and controls exactly who can read them.
Managed rotation can change credentials automatically without redeploying your app.
scenes.narration: Hardcoding a secret means it lives in your repository history indefinitely, a common source of breaches. A secrets manager encrypts values at rest and gates access through IAM. Better still, it can rotate credentials on a schedule so a leaked password quickly becomes useless.

scenes.title: Secrets Manager vs. Parameter Store
scenes.narration: AWS Secrets Manager focuses on credentials, offering automatic rotation at a per-secret cost. Parameter Store is a simpler key-value service well suited to general configuration and often free for standard parameters. Use Secrets Manager for passwords and keys, and Parameter Store for non-sensitive settings.

scenes.title: Fetching a Secret in a Pipeline
scenes.code:
import boto3, json

sm = boto3.client("secretsmanager")
resp = sm.get_secret_value(SecretId="prod/analytics-db")
creds = json.loads(resp["SecretString"])

conn = connect(host=creds["host"], user=creds["user"], password=creds["password"])
scenes.narration: This snippet shows the right way to obtain a database credential at runtime. The code calls get_secret_value with the secret's identifier and parses the returned JSON. Because the password is fetched fresh each run, rotation works transparently and no credential ever touches your source code or configuration files.

scenes.text: Never hardcode secrets — store them in a managed secrets service, fetch them at runtime, and enable rotation so a leak has a short shelf life.
scenes.narration: Keep secrets out of code entirely by storing them in a managed service and retrieving them at runtime. With rotation enabled, even a leaked credential expires quickly, sharply limiting the damage.
